The following is a [[:Category:City timelines|timeline]] of the [[History of Baku|history]] of the [[List of cities in Azerbaijan|city]] of [[Baku]], [[Azerbaijan]].
{{Dynamic list}}

==Prior to the 20th century==
{{History of Azerbaijan}}

* 12th century CE – [[Maiden Tower (Baku)]] built.
* 1169 – [[Lezgi Mosque]] built.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
* 1378 – [[Juma Mosque (Baku)|Juma Mosque]] built.<ref name=archnet>{{cite web |url= http://archnet.org/library/places/one-place.jsp?place_id=1498 |title= Baku |author=ArchNet |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20121025215019/http://archnet.org/library/places/one-place.jsp?place_id=1498 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-10-25 |author-link= ArchNet }}</ref>
* 1442 – [[Palatial mosque in Baku|Palatial mosque]] of [[Palace of the Shirvanshahs]] built.
* 1509 – Persians in power.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1578 – Ottomans in power.<ref name=iranica>{{cite encyclopedia |url=http://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/baku-pers |title=Baku |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Iranica]] |author1=S. Soucek |author2= R. G. Suny |publisher= Columbia University, Center for Iranian Studies |location=New York |access-date=30 March 2015}}</ref>
* 1603 – Persians in power again.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
* 1723 – Town [[Russo-Persian War (1722–23)|taken]] by Russians.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1732 – Oil refinery in operation.<ref name="Vassiliou2009">{{cite book|author= M. S. Vassiliou |title=Historical Dictionary of the Petroleum Industry |year= 2009|publisher=[[Scarecrow Press]] |isbn=978-0-8108-6288-3 |chapter=Chronology |chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=vArc08DO9ykC |author-link=Marius Vassiliou }}</ref>
* 1735 – Persians in power again.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1747 – [[Baku Khanate]] established.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
* 1806 – Town taken by Russian forces.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1813 – Town becomes part of [[Russian Empire|Russia]] per [[Gulistan Treaty]].{{sfn|Bosworth|2007}}
* 1817 – Cholera outbreak.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
* 1823 – Paraffin factory begins operating.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
* 1832 – "First secular Russian school" opens.<ref name=iranica />
* 1846 – Baku becomes part of the Shemakh province.<ref name=iranica />
* 1859
** Oil refineries begin operating on the outskirts of town.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
** Town becomes capital of the newly established [[Baku Governorate]].<ref name=iranica />
* 1860 – Population: 13,381.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1868
** [[Tbilisi]]-Baku telegraph begins operating.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
** [[Fountains Square, Baku|Fountains Square]] constructed.
* 1875 – ''Ekinchi'' begins publication.<ref name="Akiner2010">{{cite book|author=Shirin Akiner|title=Islamic Peoples Of The Soviet Union |year=2010|publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-14274-1}}</ref>
* 1878 – Iosif Dzahkerli becomes mayor.
* 1883 – Batum-Baku railway built.<ref name="Waal2010">{{cite book|author=Thomas de Waal |title=The Caucasus: An Introduction |year= 2010|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-974620-0 |chapter=Chronology |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=6X745rS5Ci8C |page=229+ |author-link=Thomas de Waal }}</ref>
* 1884
** {{Interlanguage link|Baku Railway Station|ru|3=Баку-Пассажирская}} built.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
** Oil Extractors Congress Council established.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}
* 1886 – Population: 45,679.<ref>{{cite book |title=Statesman's Year-Book |year=1890 |location=London |publisher= Macmillan and Co.|chapter= Russia: Principal Towns |hdl=2027/nyp.33433081590527 |title-link=Statesman's Year-Book |last1=Hunter |first1=Brian |last2=Paxton |first2=John |last3=Steinberg |first3=S. H. |last4=Epstein |first4=Mortimer |last5=Renwick |first5=Isaac Parker Anderson |last6=Keltie |first6=John Scott |last7=Martin |first7=Frederick }}</ref>
* 1887
** [[Baku Polytechnicum]] established.
** Armenian [[Saint Gregory the Illuminator's Church, Baku]] built.
* 1897 – [[List of cities of the Russian Empire in 1897|Population]]: 112,253.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
* 1900 – Population: 179,133.{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}

==20th century==

* 1901 – Synagogue built.{{sfn|Jewish Encyclopedia|1907}}
* 1902 – [[Baku International Sea Trade Port]] opens.
* 1903 – July: Labor strike.<ref name="Mostashari2006">{{cite book|author= Firouzeh Mostashari |title=On the Religious Frontier: Tsarist Russia and Islam in the Caucasus|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RBNDaEFGJrsC|year= 2006|publisher=I.B.Tauris|isbn=978-1-85043-771-0}}</ref><ref name="Cook2003">{{cite book|author1=Chris Cook|author2=John Stevenson|title=Longman Handbook of Twentieth Century Europe |year=2003|publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-89224-3 |chapter=Russian Revolution (chronology) |chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=olmPBAAAQBAJ&pg=PR13 }}</ref>
* 1904
** Balakhany and Bibi-Eibat Workers Organisation founded.<ref name="Swietochowski2004">{{cite book|author= Tadeusz Swietochowski |title=Russian Azerbaijan, 1905–1920: The Shaping of a National Identity in a Muslim Community|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cozSOSsv7ZsC|year= 2004|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-52245-8|author-link=Tadeusz Swietochowski}}</ref>
** [[Mayoralty of Baku|City hall]] built.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
* 1905
** [[Armenian–Tatar massacres of 1905–07|Armenian–Tatar massacre]].{{sfn|Britannica|1910}}
** ''Irshad'' newspaper begins publication.<ref name="Akiner2010" />
* 1907 – [[Batumi]]-Baku oil pipeline constructed.{{sfn|Dumper and Stanley|2008}}<ref>{{citation |work=Cassier's Magazine |date=November 1900 |volume=19 |title=A Russian Petroleum Pipe Line Carrying Oil from Baku to Batoum |pages=42 v |location=New York |hdl=2027/uiug.30112073488907 }}</ref>
* 1909 – [[Baku Boulevard]] constructed.
* 1910 – [[Baku Puppet Theatre|Phenomenon cinema]] built.
* 1912 – [[Azerbaijan State Philharmonic Hall|Philharmonic Hall]] built.
* 1913
** [[Ismailiyya building]] constructed.
** Population: 237,000.<ref>{{cite book |title=Statesman's Year-Book |year=1921 |location=London |publisher= Macmillan and Co.|chapter= Russia: Principal Towns: Caucasia |hdl=2027/njp.32101072368440 |title-link=Statesman's Year-Book }}</ref>
* 1914 – [[Taza Pir Mosque]] built.
* 1917 – Iranian communist [[Communist Party of Persia|Edalat Party]] founded in Baku.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Stephanie Cronin|title=Iranian-Russian Encounters: Empires and Revolutions Since 1800|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VCTipPJdKBwC|year=2013|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-0-415-62433-6 |chapter=Comintern, the Soviet Union and Labour Militancy in Interwar Iran |author=Touraj Atabaki }}</ref>
* 1918
** [[March Days]] interethnic conflict.
** [[September Days]] massacre of Armenians.
** Baku becomes capital of [[Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]].<ref name=iranica />
* 1919
** [[Baku State University]] founded.<ref name=europa2002 />
** ''Molodezh Azerbaijana'' newspaper begins publication.<ref name=europa2002 />
* 1920
** 28 April: [[11th Army (Soviet Union)]] takes city.
** Baku becomes capital of [[Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic]].<ref name="Zonn2010">{{cite book|editor=Igor S. Zonn|title= Caspian Sea Encyclopedia|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=fvqYSoRvAI4C&pg=PA61 |year= 2010|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-11524-0|display-editors=etal}}</ref>
** [[Azerbaijan State Symphony Orchestra]] and [[Azerbaijan State Oil Academy|Baku Polytechnic Institute]] founded.
** [[Azerbaijan State Academic Opera and Ballet Theater]] active.<ref name=rubin1994 />
** [[Binəqədi raion|Kirov raion]] created.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
* 1922
** 7 November: [[Arseny Avraamov|Avraamov]]'s ''Symphony of Sirens'' performed.<ref name="Curtin2014">{{cite book|author=Adrian Curtin|title=Avant-Garde Theatre Sound: Staging Sonic Modernity|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gnSEAwAAQBAJ|year= 2014|publisher=Palgrave Macmillan|isbn=978-1-137-32479-5}}</ref>
** [[Azerbaijan State Academic Drama Theatre|State Drama Theatre]] opens.<ref name=rubin1994 />
* 1923
** [[National Library of Azerbaijan]] opens on [[Nizami Street|Torgovaya]].
** [[Azerbaijan State University of Culture and Arts|Baku Theatre Technical School]] founded.<ref name=rubin1994 />
* 1925 – Baku Workers' and Peasants Theatre opens.<ref name=rubin1994 />
* 1928 – [[Azerbaijan State Theatre of Young Spectators|Theatre of Young Spectators]] founded.<ref name=rubin1994 />
* 1931 – [[Baku Puppet Theatre]] established.<ref name=rubin1994>{{cite book|editor=Ron Rubin |title=World Encyclopedia of Contemporary Theatre |year=1994 |publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-11804-3 |chapter=Azerbaijan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=klGvBAAAQBAJ |page=80 }}</ref>
* 1939 – Population: 809,347 metro.<ref name=seltzer1952>{{Citation |publisher = Columbia University Press |location = New York |editor = Leon E. Seltzer |title = Columbia Lippincott Gazetteer of the World |ol=6112221M |date = 1952 |page=146 |chapter=Baku |chapter-url= https://archive.org/stream/columbialippinco00selt#page/1250/mode/1up }}</ref>
* 1940 – Baku Museum of Education founded.<ref name=europa2002 />
* 1941 – [[Nərimanov raion|Kishlinsky district]] created.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
* 1945 – [[Azerbaijan State University of Culture and Arts|Azerbaijan State Institute for the Arts]] active.<ref name=rubin1994 />
* 1949 – [[Sumqayit]] developed near city.<ref name=seltzer1952 />
* 1951 – [[Tofiq Bahramov Stadium|Stalin Stadium]] opens.
* 1952 – [[Government House, Baku|Government House]] built.
* 1965 – Population: 737,000 city; 1,137,000 urban agglomeration.<ref>{{cite book |chapter-url= https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/products/dyb/1960_round.htm |title=Demographic Yearbook 1965 |year=1966 |publisher=[[Statistical Office of the United Nations]] |location=New York |chapter=Population of capital cities and cities of 100,000 and more inhabitants }}</ref>
* 1967
** [[Baku Metro]] begins operating.
** [[Azerbaijan Carpet Museum]] established.
* 1979 – Population: 1,046,000.<ref name="Morton1984">{{cite book|editor=Henry W. Morton and Robert C. Stuart |title=The Contemporary Soviet City|url=https://archive.org/details/contemporarysovi00mort |url-access=registration |page=[https://archive.org/details/contemporarysovi00mort/page/4 4] |year=1984|publisher=M.E. Sharpe |location=New York |isbn=978-0-87332-248-5}}</ref>
* 1985 – Population: 1,693,000 (estimate).<ref>{{cite book |chapter-url= https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/products/dyb/1980_round.htm |title=1985 Demographic Yearbook |year=1987 |author=[[United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs]], Statistical Office |location=New York |chapter=Population of capital cities and cities of 100,000 and more inhabitants |pages=247–289 }}</ref>
* 1989
** ''[[Azadliq (newspaper)|Azadliq]]'' newspaper begins publication.<ref name=europa2002>{{cite book|title=Eastern Europe, Russia and Central Asia 2003|publisher=Europa Publications |year=2002 |isbn=978-1-85743-137-7 |chapter=Azerbaijan: Directory |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EPP3ti4hysUC |page=121+ }}</ref>
** Baku Islamic Madrasa established.<ref name=Yearbook2014>{{cite book|title=Yearbook of Muslims in Europe |year= 2014|publisher=Brill|isbn=978-90-04-28305-3 |chapter=Azerbaijan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=a-NTBQAAQBAJ |page=67 }}</ref><ref name="Kemper2010">{{cite book|editor=Michael Kemper|title=Islamic Education in the Soviet Union and Its Successor States|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-gWAAgAAQBAJ|year=2010|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-134-20731-2|display-editors=etal}}</ref>
* 1990
** January:
*** [[Baku pogrom]] of Armenians.<ref name="bbc-timeline">{{cite news |url= https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-17047328 |title=Azerbaijan Profile: Timeline |work=BBC News |date=20 March 2012 |access-date= 30 March 2015 }}</ref>
*** [[Black January]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Jahanshir Afandiyev |date=18 December 2019 |title=Black January in the World Press |url=https://milliyyet.info/2019/12/18/black-january-in-the-world-press/ |publisher=Milliyyət Araşdırmalar Mərkəzi}}</ref>
** [[Sanan Alizade]] becomes mayor.
* 1991
**City becomes capital of Azerbaijan Republic.{{sfn|Bosworth|2007}}
* 1993
**[[Rafael Allahverdiyev]] becomes mayor.
* 1994
** [[1994 Baku Metro bombings]].
** [[Azerbaijan State Pantomime Theatre]] founded.
* 1995
**October: [[1995 Baku Metro fire]].
* 2000 – 25 November: The 6.8 {{M|w|link=y}} [[2000 Baku earthquake|Baku earthquake]] affected the region.

==21st century==

* 2001 – [[Hajibala Abutalybov]] becomes mayor.
* 2005 – [[Center for Economic and Social Development]] established.<ref name=ISN>{{cite web |url=http://www.isn.ethz.ch/Digital-Library/Organizations |title=Organizations |work= [[International Relations and Security Network]] |location=Switzerland |publisher=[[Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule Zürich]] |access-date= 30 March 2015 }}</ref>
* 2006
** [[Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline]] in operation.<ref name=bbc-timeline />
** [[State Maritime Administration (Azerbaijan)]] headquartered in city.
* 2008 
**December: [[International Mugham Center of Azerbaijan]] opens.
* 2009 – [[Uzeyir Hajibeyov International Music Festival]] begins.
* 2010
** [[National Flag Square]] opens in [[Bayil]].
** [[SOCAR Tower]] construction begins.
* 2012
** [[Baku Crystal Hall]] built.
** [[Heydar Aliyev Center]] opens.
** May: [[Eurovision Song Contest 2012]] held in city.
** Population: 2,122,300.
* 2013 
**[[Flame Towers]] opens.
*2014
**[[Lycée français de Bakou]] opened. Ilham Aliyev and his wife participated in the opening ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.president.az/articles/12876|title=Ilham Aliyev attended the opening of the French Lyceum of Baku|website=en.president.az|language=en|access-date=2018-12-19}}</ref>
* 2015
**[[Baku National Stadium]] opens.
** March: [[Baku Olympic Stadium]] opens.
**June: [[2015 European Games]] held in city.
